newsitem.title: UK: Ldn Freight - Negative influences prevail.
newsitem.headline: Ldn Freight - Negative influences prevail.

text.p: LONDON, Jan 23 (REUTER) - The dry cargo market still has some steady elements - Capers and Handymaxes, for example - but negative influences continue to predominate.

The BFI fell 13 points to 1422 mainly on account of the deteriorating Panamax market in the Atlantic. This has come about partly because of vessels ballasting into the US Gulf from the Far East, but also because grain charterers have relatively little to offer. The shortage of grain stems has also severely affected transatlantic rates for Handy-sizes from the US Gulf, Brazil and Argentina. The Baltic Handy Index may have remained unchanged today at 1033 but this reflects the fortune of Handymaxes only - the trial grain routes US Gulf/Continent and Brazil/Continent were marked down sharply by the panellists to $14.75 (55') and $15.88 (53') respectively.

Both US Gulf/Continent and US Gulf/Japan saw lower rates fixed today with the true extent of the weakness suspected in some cases by brokers to have been concealed. Dubrovnik, for example, was booked for 55,000 heavy grain US GUlf/Ghent by Cobelfret for early Feb at $12.00 (Zennoh berth $11.50) but it is understood the vessel will be waiting up to a week to present, and Orleta Lwowskie fixed by Klaveness for about 60,000 soyabeans US Gulf/Hamburg also at $12.00 may be cutting size to make the Hamburg arrival draft.

The 1971-built Aghias Minas, fixed by Cargill for 55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Egypt at $14.00, has agreed over-age insurance premium for owner's account. US Gulf/Japan rates were down on both voyage and timecharter. Hanjin fixed Oceanic Enterprise for 54,000 heavy grain for Feb 4/14 at $23.80 no combo ($23.95/24.00 yesterday), and Halla took Big Sky 69,000 dwt also for early Feb at $13,200 daily plus $210,000 bonus ($13,500 and $250,00 was fixed for the comparable Gortys yesterday). But Kavo Delfini (2,650,000 cft) was linked today with Cho Yang for early Feb US Gulf/Japan at $24.00 no combo. Irisl took New Paloma for 50,000/5 barley EU/Iran for early Feb at $24.75 per tonne ($26.00 for UK or Sweden).

Brokers reported that Panamax tonnage was indicating under $12.00 for Bunge's Feb 1/10 Mississippi/Holland business basis heavy grain, and Capers low $12.00's for lights (against charterer's $11.00 for both). Handy rates continued under heavy pressure with reports that Cargill had fixed US Gulf/Continent at below $12.00. This trend was seen brokers as inevitably undermining Panamax rates in these trades. Toepfer were rumoured to have fixed about 1m cft Plate/Continent at close to $22.00. this followed news that Dreyfus covered 30,000 SBM pellets 54' Brazil/Continent for Feb 5/13 at only $15.00. Groupe Pantin were said to have chartered Elena 3 26,700 dwt delivery N France prompt trip Red Sea at $10,500 daily. New business today included Goldbeam 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan March 10/22, Cargill (possibility) 25,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Klaipeda Jan 25/31 and 16,000/10 wheat Rouen/Tunisia Jan 31/Feb 7, Andre 11,500 heavy grain US Gulf/Douala Feb 5/12, Transgrain 15/20,000 heavy grain Up River/Valencia for early Feb, and Dreyfus 1/1.2m cft Paranagua or Sao Francisco do Sul/Lisbon-Hamburg range spot.

Charterers in the Atlantic were said to be splitting Caper stems into Panamax lots in search of cheaper freight. Carboex, for example, have 2 Panamax coal stems Davant/Tarragona for Feb loading, otherwise a Caper trade. Meanwhile Klaveness's fixture of Docecape 151,852 dwt delivery prompt Passero trip via Brazil to the Far East at $17,100 daily was said to have failed on subjects. In the East MOSK were linked with the Panamaxes Royal Pilot 70,000 dwt or National Prosperity 75,100 dwt for NSW coal rounds at about $11,000 daily, but Western trader 70,329 dwt was understood booked by Navix for a Cape Flattery round at only $10,850 daily. Reports circulated that Heraklia 65,159 dwt was reently booked by seatrans delivery Far East for 4-6 months but further information was lacking.
